Codex review: needs real behavior proof before merge. ## What this changes This PR centralizes durable Cron requests, execution capacity, and activation in the SQLite worker behind one host launcher. **Example:** Eight runs occupy service A while sibling service B requests report-job against the same store. - **Before:** Separate service admission counters can admit a ninth execution. - **After:** The worker queues report-job until shared capacity becomes available. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🧂 unranked krab **(1/6)** | The approved refactor has useful boundary coverage, but three availability defects and unresolved authority and existing-state evidence prevent readiness. | | **Proof confidence** | 🧂 unranked krab **(1/6)** | Real behavior proof is necessary before merge. Provide redacted terminal output or logs without credentials, IPs, phone numbers, or non-public endpoints. After adding proof, update the PR body; ClawSweeper should re-review automatically. If it does not, the PR author or someone with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review`. - [ ] **Reconcile local ownership when an activation reply is lost (P1)** - This previous finding remains present. If cron.drainQueue commits activation and its worker exits before replying, this await rejects before launch cleanup is installed. Submission has already claimed local receipt ownership, while the worker has replaced queued markers with running markers. Later drains cannot launch those rows, and same-process recovery treats the retained local claim as live. Unexecuted jobs can therefore occupy capacity indefinitely and leave accepted completion promises pending. Release or reconcile unlaunched local contexts after an uncertain activation result so recovery records interruption without replay. - [ ] **Observe completion rejections for reconstructed timed requests (P1)** - This previous finding remains present. A persisted timed request drained without a host context gets a completion promise without a consumer or rejection observer, unlike ordinary submissions. A launch or finalization failure rejects that promise in running.catch; handling running does not handle completion. An ordinary non-transient error reaches the installed unhandled-rejection handler and terminates the Gateway. Observe reconstructed completions or avoid allocating an unused rejectable promise. - [ ] **Observe the queue drain started when scheduling resumes (P1)** - When scheduling resumes with queued work, this detached drain can reject on worker admission or database failure. The surrounding synchronous try does not catch an async rejection, so an ordinary non-transient failure reaches the Gateway's fatal unhandled-rejection path. Attach a rejection handler, as the queue wake owner already does. This is a late discovery: comparison with the earlier reviewed source confirms this call was already present unchanged. - [ ] **Resolve security concern: Verify queued caller revocation before executor I/O** - The launcher retains the originating caller across acknowledgement and queue waiting, then dispatches under a detached Gateway lifetime; inspected authority tests replace execution and do not establish rejection before real I/O. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk** - Queued caller authority survives acknowledgement and detached launch; its rejection boundary for a caller revoked before capacity release remains unverified at executor I/O. - [ ] **Add data-model compatibility proof** - The review found that existing stored data may not work after upgrade.
